newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Opposition to oppose job dismissal plan.
newsitem.headline: Australia Opposition to oppose job dismissal plan.

text.p: The Australian opposition said on Tuesday it would oppose the government's move to exempt small businesses from unfair dismissal laws.
The government had been depending on Labor's support to ensure the passage of the legislation through the non-government dominated upper house of parliament, the Senate.

"The Bell Report (on small business) recommended that the Department of Industrial Relations review the government's new unfair dismissal laws after 12 months of operation," opposition industrial relations spokesman Bob McMullan said in a statement.
"There was no recommendation by Bell that small business be exempted from the unfair dismissal laws."
The exemption, which would allow businesses with up to 15 workers to dismiss employees within the first year if their work was unsatisfactory, was due to take effect from July 1.
McMullan said the government's proposal ignored employees who had a legitimate claim for unfair dismissal.
"It doesn't distinguish between claims on the basis of their merits, just on the basis of the size of the employer," he said.
The government included the exemption in its reform package for small business announced in March.
